cards.statement: In `$attrs`, Vue stores a parent's fallthrough `foo-bar` attribute under the camelCase key `fooBar`.
cards.explanation: Unlike props, fallthrough attributes keep their original casing in JavaScript, so a child reads a foo-bar attribute as `$attrs['foo-bar']`.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on vuejs.org/guide/components/attrs under 'Disabling Attribute Inheritance': 'Unlike props, fallthrough attributes preserve their original casing in JavaScript, so an attribute like foo-bar needs to be accessed as $attrs['foo-bar']'. The source anchor is correct, and the explanation does not repeat the onClick fact from sr9-11.

cards.statement: Vue delays a kept-alive component's onActivated hook until the component is re-inserted from the cache.
cards.explanation: onActivated runs on a kept-alive component's initial mount and again every time the component is re-inserted from the cache.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on vuejs.org/guide/built-ins/keep-alive, 'Lifecycle of Cached Instance': the code comment says 'called on initial mount and every time it is re-inserted from the cache', and the note says 'onActivated / activated is also called on mount'. The statement makes one false claim.

cards.statement: In Pinia, a ref that a Setup Store leaves out of its returned object still becomes part of the store's state.
cards.explanation: Pinia picks up state only from the properties a Setup Store returns, so the docs say to return every state property; leaving one out breaks SSR, devtools and plugins.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on pinia.vuejs.org/core-concepts/ (Setup Stores): 'You must return all state properties in setup stores for Pinia to pick them up as state. In other words, you cannot have private state properties in stores', and not returning them all breaks SSR, devtools and plugins. The card has the Pinia prefix and no hedge.

cards.statement: In a runtime declaration, `defineProps({ title: String })` makes title a required prop.
cards.explanation: String only declares the value type; runtime-declared props stay optional unless their declaration specifies required: true.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on vuejs.org/guide/components/props: 'All props are optional by default, unless required: true is specified', and the object-syntax example shows propA: Number next to propC: { type: String, required: true }. The runtime-declaration prefix correctly sets aside type-based declarations. The 'by default' tell is gone.

cards.statement: By default, Vue patches v-for list elements in place instead of moving them when the data order changes.
cards.explanation: Without keys, Vue keeps each DOM element at its index and updates its content: efficient, but unsafe when items hold child component state or form input values.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on vuejs.org/guide/essentials/list#maintaining-state-with-key: 'by default it uses an in-place patch strategy ... instead of moving the DOM elements to match the order of the items, Vue will patch each element in-place', and 'This default mode is efficient, but only suitable when your list render output does not rely on child component state or temporary DOM state (e.g. form input values)'. 'By default' on a true card helps balance that tell.

cards.statement: For a class panel declared in `<style module>`, `$style.panel` holds the unchanged class name panel.
cards.explanation: Vue hashes CSS Modules classes to avoid collisions, so $style.panel holds the generated class name rather than panel, which scopes the class to the current component.
cards.reason: I applied the wording lens's fix. 'By default' still leaned false across the deck (3 true / 7 false), and the assumed context (a default Vite build) already covers the generateScopedName edge case, so I removed it. The fact lens had no objection to the fact. Confirmed on vuejs.org/api/sfc-css-features#css-modules: a <style module> tag 'exposes the resulting CSS classes to the component as an object under the key of $style', and 'The resulting classes are hashed to avoid collision, achieving the same effect of scoping the CSS to the current component only.' Statement and explanation are within the length limits.

cards.statement: In a server-rendered app, renderToString() produces the rendered HTML synchronously as a plain string.
cards.explanation: renderToString() from vue/server-renderer gives a Promise that resolves to the rendered HTML, so server code awaits it.
cards.reason: Both lenses say keep. Confirmed on vuejs.org/api/ssr#rendertostring: 'Exported from vue/server-renderer', its type returns Promise<string>, and the example uses 'const html = await renderToString(app)'. The card uses the allowed SSR prefix.

cards.statement: In a `<template v-for>`, the key attribute belongs on the child elements inside the template.
cards.explanation: Vue expects the key of a <template v-for> on the <template> tag itself, because the template is the unit that repeats for each item.
cards.reason: The statement, answer and explanation are unchanged, and both lenses accept them. Confirmed on vuejs.org/guide/essentials/list#maintaining-state-with-key: 'When using <template v-for>, the key should be placed on the <template> container'. Following the wording lens's note, I set the misconception to 'Template loop keys belong on the child elements.' This drops 'as in Vue 2', which neither lens checked against a page and which counts toward the deck's three-card Vue 2 mention cap. Removing it adds no new fact.
